content: Ilex guayusa, commonly referred to as guayusa, is a tree belonging to the holly genus and is native to the Ecuadorian Amazon Rainforest. It is a distant botanical relative of both Yerba Mate and Yaupon Holly, the latter being the plant traditionally used to prepare the black drink. The leaves of guayusa contain the highest known caffeine concentration of any plant species. These leaves are typically boiled to produce a tea, and due to their high caffeine content, the same leaves are often reused multiple times, sometimes over the course of several days. Both fresh and dried leaves are utilized, with the dried leaves often prepared in rolls and strung together in a wreath-like arrangement resembling a Hawaiian lei. In addition to its stimulant properties, guayusa tea is believed to enhance dream recall. To achieve this effect, it is traditionally consumed consistently in the early morning, immediately after waking and before sunrise. Among many Ecuadorian indigenous communities, the morning consumption of guayusa tea is a deeply ingrained social ritual. In regions where the plant grows, guayusa is also commonly added to the entheogenic brew ayahuasca, either as a supplement to the more common DMT-containing plants or as a substitute for them. Indigenous Ecuadorians also claim that guayusa, when consumed in sufficiently high quantities, exhibits mild hallucinogenic properties on its own. Guayusa is commercially available under the brand name Qat Tea™, though it is unrelated to the stimulant plant known as qat.
